# Data

Two sources, never mixed. Only the synthetic one produces published results; the second is an optional local audit.

## 1. Planted synthetic world (the verification set)

**SYNTHETIC.** Generated by `attribution/world.py` and `attribution/world_events.py` from a seed (default 7), 200,000 invented users, invented channel effects, invented spend. Nothing is downloaded and no row is committed. The domain `shop.example` is a reserved example name.

- Planted truth: conversions lost when a channel is switched off, replaying the same random draws, and an exact Shapley split of that over all 128 on/off combinations of the seven switchable channels (`attribution/truth.py`).
- Only evaluation, the holdout replay and the reports read the truth. Attribution methods receive events and journeys only.
- Limits: the structure (hidden intent, early prospecting, late intent capture, positive or zero effects only, no negative effects, no cross-device gaps, no ad stock across users, no spend-response curve) is a choice made by the author. Results show what methods do **in these worlds**.
- NumPy does not promise identical random streams across all versions, so another NumPy version could change the printed numbers.

## 2. Criteo Attribution Modeling for Bidding Dataset (real, local only)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Owner | Criteo AI Lab |
| Source page | https://ailab.criteo.com/criteo-attribution-modeling-bidding-dataset/ |
| File fetched from | https://huggingface.co/datasets/criteo/criteo-attribution-dataset (the publisher's own mirror) |
| Licence | **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0**. Dataset card, read 2026-11-26: `license: cc-by-nc-sa-4.0`. The Criteo page, read the same day through a summarising fetch tool, states the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International license; its section 2(a)(1) grants use "for NonCommercial purposes only" |
| Real or synthetic | **Real** traffic: "a sample of 30 days of Criteo live traffic data", "sub-sampled and anonymized" |
| Date fetched | 2026-11-26 |
| File | `data/raw/criteo_attribution_dataset.tsv.gz`, 653,015,824 bytes |
| SHA-256 | `94ac7a465564349bc7ba008602211d5990a3c53cc133abc0aadef61ea2391a98` (matches the hash the mirror publishes for the file) |
| Size unpacked | about 2.4 GB according to the publisher. The code reads the gzip directly and never unpacks it to disk. Loading it needs a few GB of memory |
| Columns used | `timestamp, uid, campaign, conversion, conversion_timestamp, conversion_id, click` |
| Columns not read | `attribution` (the vendor's own credit decision), `click_pos`, `click_nb` (known only after the outcome), `cost`, `cpo` (transformed, not prices), `time_since_last_click`, `cat1`-`cat9` |
| Citation | Diemert, Meynet, Galland, Lefortier, "Attribution Modeling Increases Efficiency of Bidding in Display Advertising", AdKDD & TargetAd 2017 |

**What the licence means here.** Non-commercial use only. Whether a given portfolio or job-search use counts as non-commercial is a judgement this file cannot make; if in doubt, run with `--skip-criteo`. This repository publishes **no rows and no results** from the dataset. The loader is optional: its report and chart are written to the git-ignored `output/` folder. If you share them, the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms apply to them. Pseudonymous user ids stay on the local machine.

### Known biases and leakage risks

- One display vendor. `campaign` is not a marketing channel, and other channels are invisible.
- Sub-sampled, so conversion rates are not real rates.
- A path's label can depend on how the path is built. The code builds click paths only; run the audit and read how conversion labels relate to clicks before building any other kind.
- The converting and non-converting journeys are built differently: converting by conversion id, non-converting as one window per user at the end of the data. Markov and rate-game results depend on that choice.
- Changing the lookback also changes which conversions have a full window, so the lookback comparison mixes two effects.

### What it cannot answer

Which campaign caused a sale; anything about channel mix; return on spend; B2B buying; anything outside those 30 days.

## Candidates looked at and not used

Licences below were read with `kaggle datasets metadata` or the source's API on 2026-11-26.

| Candidate | Licence as listed | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| Kaggle `vivekparasharr/multi-touch-attribution` | Apache-2.0 | Downloaded and checked (10,000 rows, 2,847 users, two days). 49.4% of rows are conversions, every channel converts at 48.0% to 50.2%, and 67.6% of users have both "Yes" and "No" rows. The page does not say it is synthetic; these patterns look like independent coin flips. No usable signal |
| Kaggle `koushiktcs12/channel-attribution-modelling` | unknown | No licence, no description |
| Kaggle `kishlaya18/customer-purchase-journey-netherlands` | unknown | No licence |
| Kaggle `sonalisingh1411/fuzzy-factory-e-commerce-and-marketing-database` | CC0 (set by the uploader) | Describes an invented teddy-bear retailer, apparently teaching data re-uploaded by someone else |
| Kaggle `rifatalam3/multi-channel-e-commerce-with-behavioral-metrics` | CC0 | The listing describes customer metrics with a channel column, not ordered journeys (listing only; not downloaded) |
| Kaggle `datascikhan/tiktok-shop-viral-sales-and-cac-attribution` | CC0 | The listing shows attribution results already merged into one table; provenance could not be checked (listing only) |
| Hugging Face `lucianfialho/synthetic-attribution-benchmark` | CC BY 4.0 | Openly synthetic. Our own world was needed to control confounding and to replay holdouts |
| Zenodo 10674651, "PPRL marketing attribution" | CC BY 4.0 | Openly synthetic, built for record linkage |
| Google Analytics sample | not read | Needs a Google Cloud account |

The one extra file downloaded for checking (the first row above, about 500 kB) was kept in a temporary folder outside the project.
